newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Canada seeks to sell environment tech to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Canada seeks to sell environment tech to Argentina.

text.p: Canadian Environment Minister Sergio Marchi led a mission to sell environmental protection technology to Argentina Thursday and signed an agreement to share information with its government.

Marchi and Argentine Environment Minister Maria Julia Alsogaray, who signed a memorandum of understanding, agreed officials will meet here next February to begin cooperation on such areas as pollution prevention and toxic waste management.
Executives from two dozen Canadian environmental firms, representing Canada's fifth largest industry, travelled to pitch their knowledge in conservation.

"We believe there is an emerging market for environment technology in Latin America," Marchi told reporters. "The contracts will come. We won't know for a few months what fruit comes of the seeds we are sowing now."
Marchi, who was born in Buenos Aires, also met with Argentine Vice-President Carlos Ruckauf and Buenos Aires province Governor Eduardo Duhalde.
The Canadian mission, which already visited Brazil and Uruguay, was set to leave late Thursday for Chile.
Canadian firms will in several weeks be bidding for a waste management project, estimated at $120 million, with the municipality of Montevideo, Uruguay, Canadian officials said.
